_note: Spanish tongue twisters (trabalenguas) for /tongue-twisters, all traditional folk rhymes passed on orally, in the form usual in Spain. Each one is first read out (slowly, then at speed), then the learner repeats it and gets points per word, the same scoring as /pronunciation-check. focus: sound ids from src/lib/ausspracheTipps.js. hint: what the twister means, in simple English. Ids are the old slot ids (content-plan §1.3); this set has 20 (quality over quantity). `audio` is set to true once public/audio/zungenbrecher/<id>-langsam.mp3 and <id>.mp3 exist; until then the browser voice (es-ES) reads them. mini (optional): an animal in the twister, so a small Mini-Crew sticker (src/lib/minis.js) sits on the card. mascot (optional): the same with an animal of the crew. dialect (optional): the same twister in a regional accent, voiced as <id>-<slug(dialect.name)>.mp3, only for listening and never scored; none in this set.

sentences.text: Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal.
sentences.hint: Three sad tigers were swallowing wheat in a wheat field. This is the most famous Spanish tongue twister.

sentences.text: Pablito clavó un clavito. ¿Qué clavito clavó Pablito?
sentences.hint: Little Pablo hammered in a little nail. Which little nail did he hammer in?

sentences.text: Como poco coco como, poco coco compro.
sentences.hint: As I eat little coconut, I buy little coconut. como = as, and also I eat.

sentences.text: El hipopótamo Hipo está con hipo. ¿Quién le quita el hipo al hipopótamo Hipo?
sentences.hint: Hipo the hippo has hiccups (el hipo). Who can stop the hippo's hiccups? The h is always silent.

sentences.text: Compré pocas copas, pocas copas compré; como compré pocas copas, pocas copas pagué.
sentences.hint: I bought few glasses; as I bought few glasses, I paid for few glasses. Keep the stress on the end of compré and pagué.

sentences.text: Pancha plancha con cuatro planchas. ¿Con cuántas planchas plancha Pancha?
sentences.hint: Pancha irons with four irons. With how many irons does Pancha iron? planchar = to iron.

sentences.text: Cuando cuentes cuentos, cuenta cuántos cuentos cuentas.
sentences.hint: When you tell stories, count how many stories you tell. contar means both to tell and to count.

sentences.text: Poquito a poquito, Paquito empaqueta poquitas copitas en pocos paquetes.
sentences.hint: Little by little, Paquito packs a few little glasses in a few parcels. No puff of air after p, t or k.

sentences.text: El perro de San Roque no tiene rabo, porque Ramón Ramírez se lo ha robado.
sentences.hint: San Roque's dog has no tail, because Ramón Ramírez has stolen it. Every r at the start of a word is a trill.

es419.note: With seseo: the z of azúcar sounds like s.

sentences.text: Rápido ruedan los carros cargados de azúcar del ferrocarril.
sentences.hint: The railway's carts, loaded with sugar, roll by quickly. el ferrocarril = the railway.

es419.note: With seseo: the c of cigarro sounds like s.

sentences.text: Erre con erre, cigarro; erre con erre, barril.
sentences.hint: R with r: cigarro (cigar). R with r: barril (barrel). Both words are written with rr, and erre is the name of the letter.

es419.note: With seseo: the z of zanja sounds like s.

sentences.text: Juan junta juncos junto a la zanja.
sentences.hint: Juan gathers reeds next to the ditch. Five times the rasping j of Spain.

sentences.text: Ñoño Yáñez come ñame por las mañanas con el niño.
sentences.hint: Ñoño Yáñez eats yam (el ñame, a root vegetable) in the mornings with the child.

sentences.text: Lado, ledo, lido, lodo, ludo; decirlo al revés lo dudo. Ludo, lodo, lido, ledo, lado; ¡qué trabajo me ha costado!
sentences.hint: All five vowels, forwards and backwards. I doubt I can say it backwards… what hard work it was! Some of the first words are real (lado = side, lodo = mud), but together they mean nothing.

sentences.text: Parra tenía una perra y Guerra tenía una parra. La perra de Parra rompió la parra de Guerra.
sentences.hint: Parra had a dog and Guerra had a grapevine. Parra's dog broke Guerra's vine. Parra and Guerra are surnames; la parra is also the word for a grapevine.

sentences.text: El cielo está enladrillado. ¿Quién lo desenladrillará? El desenladrillador que lo desenladrille, buen desenladrillador será.
sentences.hint: The sky is covered with bricks. Who will take the bricks off? Whoever does will be a good un-bricker. el ladrillo = the brick.

sentences.text: Si tu gusto gustara del gusto que gusta mi gusto, mi gusto gustaría del gusto que gusta tu gusto.
sentences.hint: If your taste liked the taste my taste likes, my taste would like the taste your taste likes. An old form of gustar, with de.

sentences.text: ¿Cómo quieres que te quiera, si el que quiero que me quiera no me quiere como quiero que me quiera?
sentences.hint: How do you want me to love you, if the one I want to love me doesn't love me the way I want? querer = to want, and to love.

es419.note: With seseo every c here sounds like s, which makes this twister a different exercise.

sentences.text: Si cien sierras asierran cien cipreses, seiscientas sierras asierran seiscientos cipreses.
sentences.hint: If a hundred saws saw a hundred cypress trees, six hundred saws saw six hundred cypresses. In Spain, s and c are two sounds here: keep them apart.

es419.note: With seseo: the c of Chucena and the z of choza sound like s.

sentences.text: María Chucena su choza techaba, y un techador que por allí pasaba le dijo: María Chucena, ¿techas tu choza o techas la ajena? No techo mi choza ni techo la ajena, que techo la choza de María Chucena.
sentences.hint: María Chucena was roofing her hut. A roofer passing by asked: are you roofing your hut or someone else's? Not mine and not someone else's: I'm roofing the hut of María Chucena.
